1 General 
 
1.1 Notes on the present instructions 
The present instructions are to ensure safe and efficient handling 
of the plant. 
The instructions are an integral part of the plant; they must be 
stored in the immediate vicinity of the plant and always be 
accessible to the staff. The staff must have carefully read and 
understood the instructions before starting any work. Compliance 
with all safety and work instructions contained in the present 
instructions is an essential prerequisite for safe working. 
In addition, local accident prevention regulations and general 
safety regulations apply to the plant’s area of operation. 
Illustrations in the present instructions illustrate the general 
function and can differ from the actual design of the plant. 
 
The instructions in the Appendix covering third-party components 
shall apply in addition to the present instructions. 
 
   
 
NOTE! 
It is the owner’s obligation to store the order 
confirmation with the complete third-party 
documentation along with the present operating 
instructions in the immediate vicinity of the plant 
component.

1.2 Explanation of symbols 
 
Safety notes Symbols indicate safety notes in the present instructions. Signal 
words preceding the safety notes indicate the extent of the risk. 
It is vital to adhere to the safety notes and to act cautiously in order 
to prevent accidents, injury to persons and damage to material. 
 
  
 
DANGER! 
… indicates an immediately dangerous situation 
that, if not avoided, will cause death or severe 
injuries.   
 
 
 
WARNING! 
… indicates a potentially dangerous situation that, if 
not avoided, can cause death or severe injuries. 
 
 
 
 
CAUTION! 
… indicates a potentially dangerous situation that, if 
not avoided, can cause minor injuries. 
 
 
 
 
CAUTION! 
… indicates a potentially dangerous situation that, if 
not avoided, can cause damage to material. 
 
 
 
Tips and recommendations 
 
 
 
NOTE! 
… points out useful tips and recommendations as 
well as information necessary for efficient and 
trouble free operation.

1.3 Limitation of liability 
All information and notes in the present instructions are based on 
valid standards and regulations, current state of technology and 
our long-standing experience and expertise. 
The manufacturer will not assume liability in case of: 
 non-adherence to instructions 
 improper use 
 employment of untrained staff 
 unauthorised conversions 
 technical modification 
 use of unapproved spare parts 
The actual scope of delivery can differ from the present 
descriptions and illustrations in case of special variants, when 
additional options are ordered or because of late-breaking 
technical changes. 
The liabilities agreed in the supply contract, the General Terms and 
Conditions and the legal provisions applicable at the time of 
execution of the agreement shall apply. 
  
We reserve the right of technical modification in the context of 
improving the performance characteristics and further 
development.

The present instructions are protected by copyright and exclusively 
intended for internal purposes. 
Cession of the instructions to third persons, reproduction in any 
way or format – even partially – and utilisation and/or disclosure of 
the contents is not permitted, except for internal use, without our 
written approval. 
Noncompliance will cause indemnities. We reserve the right to 
claim additional indemnities. 
 
 
 
1.5 Spare parts 
     
 
WARNING! 
Risk of injuries due to improper spare parts! 
Improper or defective spare parts can result in 
damage, malfunction or complete failure and impair 
the safety. 
Therefore: 
– Use only genuine spare parts offered by the 
manufacturer. 
 
Purchase spare parts from an authorised dealer or directly from the 
manufacturer. Address: see cover page. 
The spare parts list is located in the Appendix. 
 
  
1.6 Warranty conditions 
 
The warranty conditions are part of the manufacturer’s General 
Terms and Conditions. 
 
 
 
1.7 Customer service 
Contact our customer service when you have technical questions. 
You can always find out the contact partner responsible for you via 
telephone, fax, email or internet, see cover page. 
Our employees are also eager to listen to your application-related 
information and experience that might prove valuable for improving 
our products.

2 Safety 
 
This section gives an overview of all safety aspects vital for an 
optimum protection of employees and for safe and trouble-free 
operation. 
Failure to comply with the safety and work instructions contained in 
the present instructions can result in severe hazards.

2.1 Limit values for magnetic field strength for th e protection of persons 
Protection against magnetic fields 
 The maximum permitted limit value for persons with an 
implanted pacemaker  is 1 mT (equal to 10 gauss). 
 This value is not exceeded at a distance ≥ 5 m to the strongest 
magnet. 
 With limited exposure time, the maximum permitted value for 
persons without implants is 2 T (20000 gauss). 
 The permitted average value for prolonged exposure (approx. 8 h)  
is 212 mT. 
 At a distance of approx. 1 m to a magnet with maxi mum 
magnetic field intensity and power of 70 kW, the maximum 
measured values were less than 100 mT. 
 
 
Protection against rotating magnetic 
fields with a frequency 
≥ 1 Hz to 30 kHz 
 The maximum permitted limit value for persons with an  
implanted pacemaker  is 0.1 mT (equal to 1 gauss).  
 This value is not exceeded at a distance ≥ 3 m to the strongest 
magnet.  
 With limited exposure time, the maximum permitted value for 
persons without implants is 0.2 T (2 gauss).  
 This value is not exceeded at a distance ≥ 1.5 m to the 
strongest magnet.

2.2 Responsibility of the owner 
 
The plant is used in an industrial environment. The owner therefore 
is subject to the legal duties of occupational safety.  
In addition to the safety notes contained in the present instructions, 
you must heed the safety, accident prevention and environment 
protection regulations. In particular: 
 The owner must inform himself of applicable indust rial safety 
regulations and must identify additional hazards resulting from 
the special work conditions in force at the plant site in a risk 
assessment. He must convert such findings into work 
instructions for operation of the plant. 
 The owner must verify whether or not the instructi ons he 
compiled comply with the current state of rules and standards 
and amend the instructions if necessary throughout the entire 
service life of the plant. 
 The owner must clearly define and assign the respo nsibilities 
for installation, operation, maintenance and cleaning. 
 The owner must make sure all employees handling th e plant 
have read and understood the operating instructions. 
He must also train the staff at regular intervals and instruct 
them with regard to the hazards. 
 The owner must provide the required personal prote ction. 
The owner is also responsible for a technically perfect condition of 
the plant at all times; the following therefore applies: 
 The owner must make sure the maintenance intervals  
mentioned in the present operating instructions are heeded. 
 The owner must have all safety devices tested for proper 
function and completeness at regular intervals.

2.3 Staff requirements 
 
2.3.1 Qualification 
  
 
WARNING! 
Risk of injury due to insufficient qualification! 
Inexpert handling can result in severe injuries and 
damage to material. 
Therefore: 
– Assign all work to qualified staff only. 
 
The operating instructions define the following qualifications for the 
various areas of operation: 
 
Only persons who may be expected to work reliably m ust be 
employed. Persons whose ability to respond is impai red, e.g. by 
narcotics, alcohol or drugs, are not allowed to work. 
 Observe the locally applicable regulations regardi ng age and 
job-related issues when choosing staff. 
 
 Instructed person  
was instructed by the owner with regard to the tasks assigned 
to him and of potential hazards in case of inexpert behaviour. 
 Specialist staff  
is capable of performing the tasks assigned to him, recognising 
and avoiding potential hazards due to his training, knowledge, 
experience and knowledge of commonly applicable regulations. 
  
 Authorised electrician  
is capable of performing work on electrical systems, recognising 
and avoiding potential hazards due to his training, knowledge, 
experience and familiarity with commonly applicable standards 
and regulations. 
The authorised electrician has been trained with regard to the 
particular site is working on and is familiar with relevant 
standards and regulations.

2.3.2 Unauthorised persons 
 
 
WARNING! 
Danger to unauthorised persons! 
Unauthorised persons not meeting the 
requirements mentioned here are not familiar with 
the hazards posed by the work area. 
Therefore: 
– Keep unauthorised persons away from the work 
area. 
– If in doubt, address persons and ban them from 
the work area. 
– Stop operation as long as unauthorised persons 
are in the work area. 
  
 
 
2.3.3 Instruction 
The owner must instruct the staff at regular intervals. For better 
traceability, the implementation of instructions must be 
documented.

2.4 Intended use 
The plant has been exclusively designed and built for the intended 
use described here. 
   
The plant is exclusively intended for grading bulk goods. For the 
properties of the bulk goods please refer to the order 
confirmation. 
 
 
 
 
WARNING!  
Beware of unintended use! 
Dangerous situations may arise when the plant is 
not operated as intended or is used for other 
purposes. 
Therefore: 
– Operate the plant as intended only. 
– Strictly adhere to all information given in the 
present operating instructions. 
– The maximum specified pole system speed 
must not be exceeded (see chapter "Setting the 
pole system speed"). 
– In particular, do not use the plant for the 
following, unintended purposes: 
– Transportation of persons 
– Walking on the conveyor 
– Material storage 
– Feed of material with incorrect or too large 
grading 
– Excess of the maximum permissible mass 
flow/flow rate 
– Feed of sticky, liquid and highly flammable 
substances 
– Iron separation 
 
 
Claims for damages of any kind resulting from unintended use are 
excluded. 
The owner is solely responsible for all damage resulting from 
unintended use.

2.5 Personal protection 
To minimise the health hazard, the use of personal protection is 
mandatory. 
 Make sure to always wear the protective equipment required for 
the respective task.  
 Heed the instructions regarding personal protectio n on display 
in the work area. 
 
Wear always Make sure to always wear: 
  
 
Protective clothing 
is closely fitting work clothing with low tensile strength, narrow 
sleeves and without protruding parts. Its main purpose is to prevent 
being caught by moving machine parts.  
Do not wear rings, chains or other jewellery. 
  
 
Safety shoes 
protect against heavy falling objects and slipping on slippery floors. 
  
 
Goggles 
protect the eyes against flying debris and splashing liquids. 
  
 
Hearing protection 
protects against hearing damage. 
  
 
Protective gloves 
protect the hands against friction, abrasion, penetration or deeper 
injuries and contact with hot surfaces. 
  
 
Breathing protection 
protects against hazardous dusts.

Wear for particular work Special protective equipment is required when performing 
particular work. Reference to such equipment is made in separate 
chapters of the present instructions. Such special protective 
equipment is explained below: 
  
 
Hard hat  
protects against falling and flying objects and material. 
  
 
Safety harness 
protects against dropping in case of increased risk of dropping. 
Such a risk is given when certain height differences have been 
exceeded and when the work place is not secured with a railing.  
Put on the safety harness so that the safety rope connects to the 
safety harness and a fixed attachment point, use a drop damper if 
necessary. 
Safety harnesses must be worn by specially trained persons only. 
  
 
 
2.6 Particular hazards 
The following section describes residual risks determined as a 
result of a risk assessment. 
 Heed the safety notes mentioned here and the warni ngs in the 
following chapters of the present instructions in order to lower 
health risks and prevent dangerous situations. 
 
 
 
Magnetic radiation 
 
 
DANGER! 
Danger of life due to magnetic radiation! 
For persons with implanted pacemaker and 
metallic implants there is a risk of severe bodily 
injury or even death in a radiation area. 
Therefore: 
– Make sure there are no persons with implanted 
pacemaker in the direct and indirect hazard 
area. 
– Make sure there are no persons with metallic 
implants in the direct and indirect hazard area.

 Safety

Electrical power 
 
 
DANGER! 
Danger of life due to electrical power! 
There is an immediate danger to life when touching 
live wires. Damage to insulation or individual parts 
can pose a hazard to life. 
Therefore: 
– When insulation damage is found, interrupt the 
power supply and have insulation repaired 
immediately. 
– Assign work on the electric system to trained 
electricians only. 
– Deenergise the electrical system and test it for 
absence of voltage before performing any work. 
– Switch off the power supply and secure it 
against switching on prior to maintenance, 
cleaning and repair work. 
– Do not bypass or disable fuses. Heed the 
correct current rating when replacing fuses. 
– Keep moisture away from live parts because it 
can cause short circuits. 
     
 
 
Noise 
 
 
WARNING!  
Hearing loss due to noise! 
The noise level present in the work area can cause 
severe hearing loss. 
Therefore: 
– Always wear hearing protection during work. 
– Restrict your stay in the danger area as far as 
possible.

Non-Ferrous Metal Separator NES 
 Safety 
 
 
21  
GB_NES 050-200 _ E50_ + NES 050-250_ E61_-03 
 
 
Highly flammable substances 
 
 
WARNING!  
Risk of fire due to highly flammable 
substances! 
Highly flammable substances, liquids or gases can 
catch fire and cause severe or even fatal injuries. 
Therefore: 
– Do not smoke in the danger area and its closer 
environment. Do not handle open fires or 
ignition sources. 
– Have fire extinguishers at hand. 
– Report suspicious substances, liquids or gases 
to the supervisor immediately. 
– Interrupt work immediately in case of a fire. 
Leave the danger area until all-clear has been 
given. 
   
 
 
Explosive dusts 
 
 
WARNING!  
Risk of explosion due to dust! 
Dust deposits can be raised and form an explosive 
mixture with ambient air. 
Therefore: 
– Smoking, handling open fires and/or ignition 
sources of all kinds is strictly forbidden in the 
area around the plant and in the hall. 
– Keep the danger area free of dust. 
– Interrupt work immediately if excessive dust 
formation occurs. Wait until the dust has settled 
and then remove the dust layer. 
   
 
 
Noxious dusts 
 
 
WARNING! 
Health risk due to dust! 
In the long term, inhaled dusts can result in lung 
damage and other health impairments. 
Therefore: 
– Always wear breathing protection during work.

Non-Ferrous Metal Separator NES 
 Safety 
 
 
22  
GB_NES 050-200 _ E50_ + NES 050-250_ E61_-03 
 
 
Moving parts 
 
 
WARNING!  
Risk of injury due to moving parts! 
Rotating and/or linear moving parts can cause 
severe injuries. 
Therefore: 
– Do not reach into/do not handle moving parts 
during operation. 
– Do not open covers during operation. 
– Observe rundown time: 
verify that all parts have stopped before you 
open covers. 
– Wear closely fitting protective clothing in the 
danger area. 
   
 
 
Vibrations 
 
 
WARNING!  
Long term injuries due to strong vibrations! 
Strong vibrations can result in long term health 
impairments. 
Vibration dampers isolate the vibration source from 
the environment. 
Therefore: 
– do not disable the vibration dampers. 
– Stay out of the vibrating area during operation. 
   
 
 
Falling material 
 
 
WARNING!  
Risk of injury due to falling material! 
Material falling down or being expelled during 
operation can cause severe injuries. 
Therefore: 
– Do not enter the danger areas while the 
automatic mode is in force. 
– Enter the danger area (e.g. during set-up) with 
hard hat, safety shoes and protective clothing 
only.

Non-Ferrous Metal Separator NES 
 Safety

Hot consumables 
 
 
WARNING!  
Risk of burns due to hot consumables! 
Consumables can reach high temperatures during 
operation, and contact with them can cause burns. 
Therefore: 
– Check whether consumables are hot before 
handling them. Let them cool down if 
necessary. 
 
 
 
Dirt and scattered objects 
 
 
CAUTION!  
Risk of stumbling due to dirt and scattered 
objects! 
Dirt and scattered objects represent slipping and 
stumbling hazards and can result in severe injuries. 
Therefore: 
– Keep the work area tidy at all times. 
– Remove objects no longer required. 
– Mark off obstacles with yellow-black marker 
tape. 
      
 
 
Sharp edges and pointed corners 
 
 
CAUTION!  
Risk of injury on edges and corners! 
Sharp edges and pointed corners can cause 
chafing of the skin and cuts. 
Therefore: 
– Take particular care when performing work next 
to sharp edges and pointed corners. 
– Wear protective gloves if you are unsure. 
   
 
 
Hot surfaces 
 
 
CAUTION!  
Risk of burns due to hot surfaces! 
Contact with hot components can cause burns. 
Therefore: 
– Always wear protective work clothing and safety 
gloves when carrying out any work near hot 
components. 
– Before performing any work, ensure that all 
components have cooled to ambient 
temperature.

2.7 Safety devices 
 
 
WARNING!  
Risk of life due to non-functioning safety 
devices! 
Only properly functioning safety devices ensure 
safety. 
Therefore: 
– Check whether the safety devices are 
functioning and correctly installed before 
starting work. 
– Never disable safety devices. 
– Make sure all safety devices such as 
emergency stop buttons, grab wires etc. are 
accessible at all times. 
 
 
 
 
NOTE! 
For more information on the position of the safety 
devices see chapter “Construction and function”.

2.9 Behaviour in case of danger or accident 
 
Preventive measures  Always be prepared for accidents and for fires! 
 Have first aid equipment (first aid kit, blankets etc.) and a fire 
extinguisher at hand. 
 Familiarise staff with accident alarm, first aid a nd rescue 
facilities. 
 Keep access paths for emergency vehicles clear. 
 
 
 
Measures in case of accidents  Immediately trigger emergency stop. 
 Initiate first aid measures.  
 Evacuate any persons from the danger area. 
 Inform the person responsible on site. 
 Alarm the rescue service. 
 Clear access paths for emergency vehicles. 
  
 
 
2.10 Environmental protection 
 
 
CAUTION! 
Environmental hazard due to inexpert handling! 
Inexpert handling of substances harmful to the 
environment, in particular inexpert disposal, can 
result in considerable environmental damage. 
Therefore: 
– Make sure to always heed the instructions 
below. 
– Take suitable measures immediately if 
substances harmful to the environment are 
released inadvertently. If in doubt, inform the 
responsible local authorities of the damage. 
 
 
The following substances harmful to the environment are being 
used: 
 
 
Lubricants 
 
Lubricants such as grease and oil contain noxious substances. 
They must not reach the environment. Disposal must be performed 
by a waste management company.

2.11 Labelling 
There are following symbols and information signs in the work 
area. They refer to the immediate vicinity of the place where they 
are affixed. 
 
 
WARNING!  
Risk of injury due to unreadable symbols! 
Decals and signs can become soiled or unreadable 
due to other circumstances in the course of time. 
Therefore: 
– Keep all safety, warning and operating notes in 
a clearly legible condition at all times. 
– Replace damaged signs or decals immediately. 
  
 
 
 
 
Heed the operating instructions 
Use the identified object only when you have read the operating 
instructions. 
  
 
 
 
 
No access for unauthorised persons 
Only persons authorised by the owner may enter the danger area. 
  
 
 
 
 
Fall hazard 
Be careful when entering a danger zone. 
Put on the safety harness or appropriate protective clothing if 
necessary. 
  
 
 
 
 
Electrical power 
Only trained electricians are allowed to work in rooms marked with 
this sign. 
Unauthorised persons are not allowed to enter work stations or 
open switch cabinets identified accordingly.

Hot surface 
Hot surfaces such as hot machine parts, containers or materials 
but also hot surfaces are not always identifiable. Do not touch 
these without protective gloves. 
  
 
 
 
 
Falling objects 
Work in areas identified by this symbol must be performed under 
an overhead guard or safety scaffold only. This does not exempt 
from the obligation to wear a hard hat. 
Avoid a stay in the area identified by this symbol. 
Objects can fall down during operation, in particular when the 
power supply fails. 
   
 
 
 
 
Magnetic field 
Magnetic fields as such are not dangerous to persons but strong 
magnetic fields can erase audio and data tapes, data memories 
and magnet strips on bank and identification cards. 
Eddy currents resulting from alternating magnetic fields can heat 
up metallic objects considerably. This also applies to jewellery 
such as rings or watches. 
Keep metallic objects away from areas marked with this symbol. 
  
 
 
 
 
No persons with pacemakers 
Strong electromagnetic or magnetic fields in the area around this

4.2 Brief description 
  
The non-ferrous metal separator functions according to the eddy 
current principle. It is distinguished by its adjustable, eccentric 
magnet pole system.  
The non-ferrous metal separator comprises a rapidly rotating 
permanent magnet pole system. The fast alternating frequency of 
the magnetic field causes strong eddy currents in the non-ferrous 
metal parts which, in turn, create magnetic fields with a repulsing 
effect to the external magnetic fields. The non-ferrous parts are 
repulsed and ejected from the remaining material flow.  
 
 
The non-ferrous metal separator can be equipped with the 
following options: vibration monitor, skewing switch on the 
conveyor belt, fast-acting brakes (electric/mechanic) and/or 
electronic frequency converters for pole system and conveyor belt 
speed.

7.3 Adjustment of non-ferrous metal separator 
 
7.3.1 General 
 
Principle 
The material on the conveyor belt reaches the pole drum in the 
area of the rapidly rotating pole system. Eddy currents are induced 
in electrical conductors. These eddy currents accelerate particles 
in the conveying direction, ejecting the particles from the material. 
The particle reaches the area downstream of the splitter. No eddy 
currents are formed in non-conducting material (rubber, wood, 
etc.). Particles of such material drop in front of the splitter in the 
normal vertically parabolic trajectory. 
 
 
General information on the material 
Grading the material into particle size fractions increases the 
efficiency of the non-ferrous materials separator considerably 
because there is no overlapping of small non-ferrous particles with 
large-surface rubber particles. Furthermore, the separator splitter 
can be better adjusted to the vertically parabolic trajectory, 
especially for fine-grained particles. 
 
 
System position 
Acceleration of non-ferrous particles basically occurs tangentially 
to the system, i.e. at 0 degrees the particles fly away almost 
horizontally. These particles cover the greatest distance. But the 
accelerated particles can also carry away rubber particles lying in 
front of them. Select this position if all non-ferrous particles are to 
be separated from the material flow as far as possible and if purity 
of the material is of secondary importance. 
The distance covered becomes shorter when the angle increases, 
but then the rubber particles reach the curved area of the conveyor 
and start slipping. Following non-ferrous metal particles can then 
be accelerated without being impeded by the rubber particles. This 
setting is recommended if a clean non-ferrous product is desired.  
 
 
 
NOTE! 
The manufacturer recommends setting a higher 
degree with smaller particle sizes.

Initial filling

Relubrication 
 
 
NOTE!

– ambient temperatures above + 40 ° C 
– high dust load 
– high moisture and similar 
the bearings should be lubricated every 40 operating hours.

grease appears at the lubricating gap.

Replacing the grease filling 
The bearing manufacturer recommends replacing the old grease 
with new grease after approx. 2000 operating hours, but at the 
latest after 1.5 years. This does not necessarily require a 
disassembly of the bearings. It is sufficient to relubricate until all of 
the old grease has been pushed out of the housing. For 
manufacturer approved grease types and volumes, see 
“Consumables”. 
 
Replacing the grease filling in case of a repair 
Fill only 30 to 50% of the bearing space with new grease. Too 
much grease will result in too high operating temperatures of the 
bearings. Apply a generous amount of grease on all sealing lips. 
For manufacturer approved grease types and volumes, see 
“Consumables”. 
 
Longer standstill of the plant 
Relubricate if a longer standstill period (> 4 months) is planned.  
Relubricate again shortly before restarting the plant after a longer 
standstill period. For manufacturer approved grease types and 
volumes, see “Consumables”.
